title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is an abelian variety over a field of characteristic p. The previous page introduces 'anti-polarizations' φ, isogenies A → A* whose transpose is φ' = −φ (Grothendieck's sign convention). For such φ it sets δ(φ) = √deg φ and Δ(φ) = α_p(φ), a p-adic determinant of T_p(φ) on the étale part. The goal is that Δ(φ)/δ(φ) is independent of the choice of φ. Writing ψ = φ∘u with u ∈ E = End(A)⊗Q symmetric for the Rosati involution (u' = φ u φ^{-1}), this reduces to Δ(u) = δ(u). The previous page already obtains Δ(u)² = deg u, so Δ(u) = ±δ(u), and the sign is left open.

This page is an abandoned, crossed-out attempt to fix that sign.
(1) By the p-adic analogue of Weil's characteristic-polynomial theorem, one would have (*) deg u = det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u*)_ét, the étale part of A and the étale part of A* (dual of the multiplicative part of A).
(2) It would then remain to show (1°) that the étale determinants of u on A and of u* on A* agree, and (2°) that the sign ε(u) is +1.
(3) The margin restates the target as det T_p(u) = ε(u)·√deg u with ε(u) = ±1.
(4) Strategy for the sign: restrict to invertible symmetric u in E = Hom(A,A)⊗Q. Then ε : E* → {+1, −1} is a ratio of two polynomial-type functions (Δ and √deg), hence a rational function with values ±1. So it is continuous and locally constant, and the plan is to compare two functions that agree.

The next page carries out the cleaner version. Δ(u) is a polynomial in the coordinates of u with integer values on integral points, hence has rational (p-integral) coefficients. Positivity on the cone u > 0 can be checked after a real embedding. There a positive u is w² with w hermitian, so Δ(u) = Δ(w)² ≥ 0, which forces ε = +1 on positive elements.

What it serves: a canonical p-adic square root of the degree of a polarization, i.e. a canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A*)_ét induced by a polarization. This is part of the 1969 Barsotti–Tate/crystal program on polarized p-divisible groups. The analogous sign phenomenon on the coherent side is Mumford's χ(L) = ±√deg φ_L, which is positive for ample L.
errors: (*) cannot hold as an equality of numbers. deg u is a positive integer while the right side lies in Z_p and is only defined up to p-adic units. At best it says the p-adic valuations agree.

Even valuation-wise, (*) ignores the local-local (connected with connected dual) part of A[p^∞], which also contributes to the p-part of deg u. It fails for non-ordinary A; e.g. for supersingular A both étale parts vanish. The same issue affects the claim on the next page that ν_p(card Coker T_p(φ)_ét) = ν_p(√deg φ). This is plausibly why the passage was crossed out.
1°) is written as an equality of maps T_p(u)_ét = T_p(u*)_ét between different modules. Only an equality of determinants (via the identification induced by φ) makes sense.
The sign argument on this page is incomplete (locally constant rational function, unfinished). It is superseded by the positivity argument on the next page.

ideas.what: For a Rosati-symmetric u, the p-adic determinant of u on Tate modules is a square root of deg u, determined up to sign. The sign is shown to be +1 on positive elements by writing u = w².
ideas.modern_name: Canonical square root / Pfaffian of the degree of a polarization; reduced norm of symmetric elements of End⁰(A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fact that deg of a polarization is a square: Mumford (Riemann–Roch, deg φ_L = χ(L)²), Weil. Positivity of Rosati: Weil.

ideas.what: p-part of the degree read off from étale parts of A and A* (a p-adic analogue of Weil's deg u = P_u(0))
ideas.modern_name: Degree of an isogeny via Dieudonné modules / Tate modules of the étale and multiplicative parts of A[p^∞]

ideas.what: Sign function ε : (E^sym)* → {±1} shown constant on the positive cone by a rationality/continuity argument
ideas.modern_name: Sign character on symmetric units of a semisimple algebra with positive involution

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out working draft of a standard argument (the degree of a symmetric isogeny is a square; the sign is fixed by Rosati positivity), applied to p-adic étale determinants. The only mildly notable feature is the aim of a canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A*)_ét induced by a polarization. That aim is flawed for non-ordinary A, and nothing here seems absent from the literature in a way specialists would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line (*) reads 'deg u = det T_p(u)_ét  det T_p(u*)_ét,' with no explicit product dot.
'E* → (+1, −1)' is meant as a map to the sign group {±1}.
The crossed-out bottom-left word is plausibly 'identiques' rather than 'intègres' ('… deux fonctions identiques').
'paire' is likely 'pair' (even function) or part of 'pair et une fonction rationnelle'.
The opening crossed line is likely '[…] T_p(u) et T_p(u*) sont […] de forme…'; 'Lorsque' is uncertain.
Marginal bracket: '[justification de …]' leading into 'D'ailleurs on peut se borner à supposer…'.
